rows.predictor: rear_Cs_at_start_of_rearing used directly as the absolute assigned starting rearing-brood size in chicks; coefficient is the adjusted change in brood-mean day-14 weight for +1 chick, conditional on rear_d0_rear_nest_brood_size and hatch_year

rows.note: Native-scale focal effect: -1.07428 g (SE 0.09254 g), Wald z = -11.6085 with asymptotic standard-normal inference (no finite denominator df). Gaussian identity-link GEE fitted to all 3,720 chicks alive and measured at day 14 in 453 year-specific rearing-brood clusters. The model included categorical rearing treatment and categorical breeding year, used an exchangeable within-rearing-brood working correlation, and brood-clustered sandwich standard errors. Observation unit: chick; exposure and clustering unit: rearing brood identified by hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID. Design: brood-size manipulation; all enlarged, reduced, and unmanipulated categories were included. The focal signed contrast is adjusted expected day-14 weight for rear_nest_trt=5 (enlarged) minus rear_nest_trt=6 (reduced); the unmanipulated category has contrast weight zero. No sample rows were excluded. The negative estimate means lower day-14 mass under greater sibling competition.
rows.predictor: Adjusted expected day-14 weight contrast: rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged brood) minus rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced brood), with the unmanipulated category assigned contrast weight 0

stats.unit: chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Outcome: arithmetic mean day-14 tarsus length (mm) among measured chicks within each rearing brood. Observation/analysis unit: rearing brood, uniquely identified as hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID; broods were equally weighted. Model: ordinary least squares, mean_day14_tarsus ~ competition_score + categorical hatch_year, with conventional model-based OLS SE. Included all 453 treatment-classified rearing broods (166 reduced, 120 unmanipulated, 167 enlarged) and all 3,720 chicks with complete day-14 tarsus measurements; rows lacking year, rearing-nest ID, treatment classification, or tarsus would have been excluded (none of the measured outcome rows relevant to these 453 broods were missing). Design: three-group brood-size manipulation represented by an ordered linear contrast. Test statistic: t = -8.243101892807; inferential residual df = 449. The coefficient is mm per one score step and assumes equal spacing from reduced to unmanipulated and from unmanipulated to enlarged; it was not converted to the two-step enlarged-minus-reduced difference.
rows.predictor: competition_score constructed from rear_nest_trt as -1 = reduced (code 6), 0 = unmanipulated (code 7), +1 = enlarged (code 5); coefficient is the adjusted change in rearing-brood mean day-14 tarsus length in mm per +1 score step

stats.unit: rearing brood, identified by hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID

rows.note: Outcome: individual day_14_weight (grams). Analysis included 2,801 chicks alive and measured at day 14 from 333 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (167 enlarged, 166 reduced). Unmanipulated broods (rear_nest_trt=7), treatment codes outside 5/6, and observations missing fitted variables were excluded. Model: Gaussian linear mixed-effects model on the identity scale, fitted by REML, with a random intercept for rearing brood (uniquely constructed as hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID) and categorical breeding-year fixed effects; model-based SE. Observation unit: chick; exposure and dependence unit: rearing brood. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation comparing enlarged with reduced broods. Focal test: Wald z = -11.409554538400112, with asymptotic standard-normal inference and no finite denominator df. The model converged. Estimated rearing-brood random-intercept variance = 0.6513402476055725, residual variance = 0.5840726365699429, implied ICC = 0.5272247488662555. The estimate is the adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in expected day-14 mass, in grams.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: indicator coded 1 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

stats.unit: chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Outcome: individual chick day_14_weight in grams. Model: unadjusted Gaussian identity-link generalized estimating equation, day_14_weight ~ enlarged_vs_reduced, with exchangeable working correlation for chicks within the same rearing brood and brood-clustered sandwich standard errors; no covariates. Focal estimate is the enlarged-minus-reduced difference in expected day-14 mass. Test: Wald z = -11.573660088399677; inferential df: no finite denominator df (asymptotic standard-normal inference). Fitted n = 2,801 chicks in 333 rearing-brood clusters (167 enlarged, 166 reduced). Observation unit: chick alive and measured at day 14. Exposure/cluster unit: rearing brood, identified as hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID because numeric nest IDs recur across years. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation comparing enlarged with reduced broods. Excluded unmanipulated rear_nest_trt=7 broods, records outside treatment codes 5/6, and records missing fitted variables. The fitted working within-brood correlation was 0.5395799443901118. Estimate and SE remain in the model's native gram scale.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: indicator coded 1 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is enlarged minus reduced

stats.unit: chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Year-adjusted OLS fitted to 453 equally weighted rearing broods (3,720 contributing chicks). Outcome: mean day_14_tarsus_length in mm among chicks alive and measured at day 14 within each rearing brood. Observation/assignment unit: rearing brood identified by hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID. Predictor: ordered three-group brood-size-manipulation score, with categorical hatch_year adjustment. Conventional model-based OLS SE; t = -8.243101892807 with 449 residual df. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation, using reduced, unmanipulated, and enlarged groups and imposing a linear, equally spaced treatment-score effect. No outcome or predictor missingness exclusions beyond requiring identifiable year/rearing nest, recognized treatment code, and measured tarsus; all 453 represented broods were fitted.
rows.predictor: competition_score coded exactly as -1 for experimentally reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=6), 0 for unmanipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=7), and +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5); coefficient is mm of brood-mean day-14 tarsus length per one-score-step increase

stats.unit: rearing brood identified by hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, aggregated to one equally weighted observation per rearing brood. Rearing broods were identified by the composite hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID because nest IDs can recur across years. Analysis included rear_nest_trt=5 enlarged broods and rear_nest_trt=7 unmanipulated broods; rear_nest_trt=6 reduced broods and rows outside focal treatment codes were excluded. Fitted model: OLS mean_day14_weight ~ enlarged_vs_unmanipulated + categorical hatch_year, using conventional model-based OLS uncertainty. Native focal effect = -0.9027126 grams, SE = 0.1146579 grams; t = -7.8730962 with 283 residual df. Fitted n = 287 rearing broods (167 enlarged, 120 unmanipulated), containing 2,661 measured chicks. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: enlarged-versus-unmanipulated brood comparison with breeding-year fixed effects. The unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods in clutch size or laying date, so this contrast has weaker causal identification than a comparison wholly within the randomized manipulation.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_unmanipulated indicator: 1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt=7 (unmanipulated rearing brood); coefficient is the year-adjusted enlarged-minus-unmanipulated difference in brood-mean day-14 mass

rows.note: Chick-level OLS: day_14_weight (grams) ~ enlarged_vs_reduced + categorical hatch_year. The observation unit was the individual chick; outcomes were not aggregated. Analysis included 2,801 chicks from 333 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (167 enlarged, 166 reduced) and excluded unmanipulated broods (rear_nest_trt=7) and rows outside treatment codes 5/6. Covariance was clustered by the year-specific rearing-brood identifier (hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID), with the small-sample cluster correction and t reference distribution. Focal test: t=-11.352429664496778 with 332 inferential df. The estimate and SE are in the native outcome scale of grams. Design: experimentally assigned brood enlargement versus reduction, analyzed with breeding-year fixed effects. The fitted sample consists of chicks alive and measured at day 14, so inference is conditional on that represented frame.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: indicator coded 1 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is the year-adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in individual day-14 weight

rows.note: Outcome: individual day_14_weight in grams. Model: unadjusted chick-level OLS, day_14_weight ~ competition_contrast, restricted to experimentally enlarged (rear_nest_trt=5) and reduced (rear_nest_trt=6) broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded. Uncertainty: finite-sample-corrected sandwich standard error clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID, with t inference using 331 df (number of 332 brood clusters minus 1). Native effect = -1.01408397108 g, SE = 0.089465610763 g; t = -11.334902455. Fitted n = 2,801 chicks (1,742 in enlarged and 1,059 in reduced broods), clustered in 332 rearing broods. Observation unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation. The chick-level fit weights broods in proportion to their number of measured day-14 chicks and therefore targets the average measured chick.
rows.predictor: competition_contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); the coefficient is the unadjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in individual day-14 mass

stats.unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Native-scale effect in grams from 332 equally weighted rearing-brood means (2,801 day-14 chick measurements): 167 enlarged and 165 reduced broods; unmanipulated broods excluded. Outcome was mean day_14_weight within rear_nest_breed_ID. No covariate adjustment. Welch heteroskedastic uncertainty gave t = 11.5128324911 with Satterthwaite df = 276.903268696 (two-sided p = 2.5301673957e-25). Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation. Group means were 9.70123106464 g enlarged and 10.7822087542 g reduced. Because the predictor is +1 versus -1, the reported coefficient is half the reduced-minus-enlarged mean difference; its SE is likewise half the Welch SE for that difference.
rows.predictor: competition-relief contrast coded +1 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced brood; less sibling competition) and -1 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged brood; more sibling competition); coefficient = (mean reduced - mean enlarged)/2

rows.note: Outcome: within-rearing-brood arithmetic mean of day_14_tarsus_length (mm). Observation unit: rearing brood identified by rear_nest_breed_ID. Included 332 experimentally manipulated broods (167 enlarged, 165 reduced), comprising 2,801 chicks measured at day 14; excluded unmanipulated broods. Model: brood-level OLS adjusted for categorical breeding year, where year was the unique within-brood modal hatch_year; HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust SE with t inference. Native effect = -0.389111 mm, SE = 0.045857 mm; t(328) = -8.48535. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation with equal weighting of broods.
rows.predictor: Competition contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced brood); coefficient is the breeding-year-adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in brood-mean day-14 tarsus length.

rows.note: Outcome: mean day-14 weight (grams) among measured chicks within each year-specific rearing brood, giving each brood equal weight. OLS model: mean_day14_weight ~ categorical rearing-brood group + categorical breeding year + rearing-nest clutch size + rearing-nest laying date. Focal signed contrast weights on adjusted group means were enlarged=+1, reduced=-0.5, unmanipulated=-0.5. Test statistic: t=-12.254839970212608; inferential residual df=440. Fitted n=447 rearing broods (165 enlarged, 166 reduced, 116 unmanipulated), containing 3,668 measured chicks. Observation unit: year-specific rearing brood. Design: brood-size manipulation with all three categories modeled categorically. Excluded treatment codes outside 5/6/7 and broods missing outcome, year, clutch size, or laying date. Native effect and SE are in grams. Interpretive limitation: unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, so the composite contrast partly relies on covariate adjustment.
rows.predictor: Adjusted mean day-14 mass contrast: enlarged rearing broods minus the equally weighted average of reduced and unmanipulated rearing broods; exact weights enlarged=+1, reduced=-0.5, unmanipulated=-0.5

rows.note: Day-14 mass was averaged within each rearing brood (rear_nest_breed_ID), and the 120 unmanipulated broods were excluded. The fitted sample comprised 332 experimentally manipulated rearing broods (167 enlarged, 165 reduced) and 2,801 chick measurements. The analysis estimated enlarged-minus-reduced differences separately within breeding years 2001, 2002, and 2003, then weighted them by each year's share of the 332 manipulated broods. Brood year was the unique modal hatch_year among a brood's chicks. Uncertainty used the Neyman design-based variance from treatment-arm variances within years and normal z inference. Native effect = -1.08206150439 g; SE = 0.0937252600877 g; z = -11.5450360274; inferential df = not applicable (normal randomization-based approximation). Observation unit: rearing brood represented by its mean mass among chicks alive and measured at day 14. Design: two-arm brood-size manipulation with breeding-year stratification and equal weighting of broods within the year-standardized contrast.
rows.predictor: Competition contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced); reported effect is the manipulated-brood-year-share-weighted average of within-year enlarged-minus-reduced differences in rearing-brood mean day-14 mass

stats.unit: rearing brood represented by its mean mass among chicks alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Outcome: individual day_14_weight in grams. Model: chick-level OLS of day-14 mass on continuous net_rearing_manipulation plus categorical hatch_year. Included chicks were alive and measured at day 14, assigned to experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt 5 or 6), and had nonmissing mass, hatch year, rearing-brood ID, and manipulation dose; unmanipulated broods and missing-dose records were excluded. Uncertainty: finite-sample-corrected heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID, with t inference. Native effect = -0.167008 g per net chick; SE = 0.0144914 g per net chick; t = -11.5246; inferential df = 318. Fitted n = 2,716 individual chicks in 319 rearing-brood clusters. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear dose-response; chicks are weighted equally. Observed dose range was -4 to +4. The result is conditional on survival and measurement at day 14 and assumes a linear dose-response over that range.
rows.predictor: net_rearing_manipulation, constructed as the number of chicks moved into the rearing brood minus the number moved out (negative = experimentally reduced; positive = experimentally enlarged); coefficient is the year-adjusted change in individual day-14 mass, in grams, per one additional net chick

rows.note: Outcome: individual chick day-14 mass (grams), among chicks alive and measured at day 14. Analysis included 2,801 chicks from the experimentally manipulated arms only (1,742 chicks in 167 enlarged rearing broods; 1,059 chicks in 165 reduced rearing broods); 120 unmanipulated broods were excluded because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. Model: unadjusted chick-level OLS of day_14_weight on the signed treatment contrast, with an intercept. Uncertainty: sandwich standard error clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID with finite-sample correction. Native effect = -1.01408397108 g; SE = 0.089465610763 g; t = -11.334902455 with 331 inferential df (332 rearing-brood clusters minus 1). Fitted n = 2,801 chicks. Observation unit = individual chick; treatment-assignment and uncertainty-clustering unit = rearing brood. Design = two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation. The estimate is chick-weighted and equals mean mass in enlarged broods (9.76268656716 g) minus mean mass in reduced broods (10.7767705382 g).
rows.predictor: Sibling-competition treatment contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); the reported coefficient is exactly the enlarged-minus-reduced difference in individual-chick mean day-14 mass.

rows.note: Outcome: individual chick day_14_weight in grams. Analysis included chicks alive and measured at day 14 in experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods, excluding unmanipulated broods, treatment codes outside 5/6, and records missing outcome, identifiers, rear_nest_CS, or rear_nest_LD. Model: Gaussian identity-link GEE with exchangeable within-rearing-brood working correlation and brood-clustered sandwich SE. Covariates were linear rear_nest_CS and rear_nest_LD, both pre-manipulation rearing-nest variables centered at analytic chick-row means 10.6899029823931 and 16.863456701401365, respectively. Rearing-brood clusters were identified by hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID. Fitted n=2,783 chicks in 331 rearing broods (165 enlarged, 166 reduced). Observation unit: chick; exposure and clustering unit: rearing brood. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation via cross-fostering. Native focal effect=-1.0782957759234733 g, SE=0.09238457265383644 g; Wald z=-11.67181646186567; inferential df: no finite denominator df (asymptotic standard-normal inference). Working exchangeable correlation=0.5391527523327322.
rows.predictor: enlarged_vs_reduced: indicator coded 1 when rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and 0 when rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is the covariate-adjusted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in expected day-14 chick weight

stats.unit: chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Native effect: -0.1427209 g; SE 0.0899431 g. Test statistic: t = -1.5867906 with 284 residual df. Fitted n = 286 rearing broods (166 experimentally reduced and 120 unmanipulated), containing 1,978 chicks measured at day 14. Observation unit: rearing brood, identified by hatch_year jointly with rear_nest_breed_ID because numeric nest IDs recur across years. Outcome: median day_14_weight among measured chicks in each brood. Model: conventional unadjusted brood-level OLS, median_day14_weight ~ unmanipulated_vs_reduced. Design: comparison of experimentally reduced broods with unmanipulated broods; enlarged broods were excluded. Rows outside rear_nest_trt codes 6/7 and incomplete fitted variables were excluded (the fitted outcome was complete). The coefficient is the unmanipulated-minus-reduced difference in brood-median day-14 mass. No hatch-year adjustment was used. Important limitation: unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods, so this is not a clean randomized treatment contrast.
rows.predictor: unmanipulated_vs_reduced = 1 for rear_nest_trt 7 (unmanipulated brood) and 0 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced brood); coefficient is 1 minus 0

rows.note: Gaussian identity-link GEE fitted to individual chick day-14 weight (grams), with recorded net_rearing_manipulation as a linear continuous predictor and categorical hatch year as an adjustment. An exchangeable working correlation was used within composite year-by-rearing-nest brood clusters, with brood-cluster robust sandwich uncertainty. The fitted sample was 2,716 measured chicks in 320 experimentally enlarged or reduced rearing broods; unmanipulated broods were excluded, as were 85 chick rows in manipulated broods lacking recorded net manipulation. Observation unit: individual chick. Design: brood-size manipulation analyzed as a chick-level, chick-weighted GEE. Native effect = -0.1799499482 grams per net chick added; robust SE = 0.0148866177 grams; Wald z = -12.0880344888; inferential df = infinite (asymptotic normal inference).

rows.note: Chick-level OLS of day_14_weight (grams) on competition_score and categorical hatch_year. competition_score was +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5) and -1 for experimentally reduced broods (rear_nest_trt=6); unmanipulated broods were excluded. CR1 finite-sample-corrected standard errors were clustered by year-specific rearing brood (hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID). Native effect = -0.508069880305 g per 1-unit score increase; cluster-robust SE = 0.0447542856745 g; t = -11.3524296645; inferential df = 332 (333 brood clusters); fitted n = 2,801 chicks. Observation unit: chick alive and measured at day 14. Design: brood-size manipulation comparing experimentally enlarged with reduced rearing broods, adjusted for categorical breeding year.
rows.predictor: competition_score: +1 for rear_nest_trt=5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -1 for rear_nest_trt=6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is grams per 1-unit increase, so the full enlarged-minus-reduced contrast spans 2 units

stats.unit: chick alive and measured at day 14

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, aggregated to one equally weighted observation per rearing brood. Included broods assigned to enlarged (rear_nest_trt=5) or reduced (rear_nest_trt=6) treatment; composite brood ID was hatch_year:rear_nest_breed_ID. Exposure was reconstructed from movement bookkeeping as rear_Cs_in minus rear_Cs_out. It exactly matched net_rearing_manipulation wherever both were observed. Of 333 assigned enlarged/reduced broods, 13 lacked reconstructable exposure and were excluded; the fitted sample comprised 320 broods and 2,716 chick measurements. Model: OLS of brood-mean day-14 weight on reconstructed signed net chick movement and categorical hatch year, using conventional model-based OLS uncertainty. Native effect = -0.1823279393 grams per additional net chick added; SE = 0.0156424771; t=-11.6559505551 with 316 residual df. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed as a linear dose-response, adjusted for breeding year. Unmanipulated broods were not included because they were not systematically matched to manipulated broods.

rows.note: Outcome: median day-14 tarsus length (mm) among measured chicks within each rearing brood. Observation unit and fitted n: 453 rearing broods, uniquely identified as hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID; these summarized all 3,720 measured chicks (166 reduced, 120 unmanipulated, 167 enlarged broods). Model: equal-brood-weight ordinary least squares, median_day14_tarsus ~ competition_score + categorical hatch_year, using the conventional model-based OLS standard error. Focal test: t = -7.606476565027 with 449 residual inferential df. Design: three-group brood-size manipulation represented by an ordered linear contrast. No outcome values were missing; rows lacking year or rearing-nest identity would have been excluded. The coefficient is in the native fitted scale of mm per one score step and assumes the reduced-to-unmanipulated and unmanipulated-to-enlarged steps are equally spaced in sibling competition.
rows.predictor: competition_score, coded exactly as -1 for experimentally reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=6), 0 for unmanipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=7), and +1 for experimentally enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5); reported coefficient is the linear change in brood-median day-14 tarsus length in mm per +1 score step

stats.unit: rearing brood, identified by hatch_year x rear_nest_breed_ID

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, aggregated so each year-specific rearing brood received equal weight. Model: OLS of brood-mean day-14 weight on competition_score plus categorical hatch_year. Groups included: 167 enlarged, 166 reduced, and 120 unmanipulated rearing broods; no treatment group was excluded. Fitted n=453 rearing broods representing 3,720 chicks. Observation unit: year-specific rearing brood, constructed as hatch_year × rear_nest_breed_ID because bare nest IDs recur across years. Design: brood-size manipulation experiment with the unmanipulated category included in an ordered linear contrast; unmanipulated broods were not systematically matched to manipulated broods. The score assumes unmanipulated broods are the midpoint between enlarged and reduced treatment-category scores. Native effect=-0.543029125665 grams per one-unit score increase; model-based SE=0.0475161924807 grams; t=-11.4282962779 with 449 residual df. This is a signed linear trend, not an omnibus statistic and not the full two-unit enlarged-minus-reduced difference.
rows.predictor: competition_score: +1 for enlarged rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=5), 0 for unmanipulated rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=7), and -1 for reduced rearing broods (rear_nest_trt=6); coefficient is grams per one-unit increase in this ordered score

rows.note: Outcome: individual chick day_14_weight in grams. Observation unit: each chick alive and measured at day 14 with nonmissing net_rearing_manipulation; fitted n=2,716 chicks in 319 rearing-brood clusters. Exclusions: unmanipulated rear_nest_trt=7, chicks outside experimentally enlarged/reduced rear_nest_trt 5/6, and rows missing outcome, hatch_year, rearing-brood ID, or manipulation dose. Model: chick-level OLS day_14_weight ~ net_rearing_manipulation + net_rearing_manipulation^2 + categorical hatch_year. Uncertainty: finite-sample-corrected standard errors clustered by rear_nest_breed_ID, with t inference; t=-11.5041676116, inferential df=318. Design: experimental brood-size manipulation analyzed with a quadratic dose-response. The focal native-scale contrast is fitted mass at dose +2 minus fitted mass at dose -2, holding breeding year fixed; the quadratic and year terms cancel in this symmetric contrast. Dose was net_rearing_manipulation, defined as chicks moved in minus chicks moved out. The fitted estimate indicates 0.66094 g lower day-14 mass at +2 than at -2 net chicks.
rows.predictor: Model-implied day-14 mass contrast for net_rearing_manipulation=+2 minus net_rearing_manipulation=-2, where net_rearing_manipulation is chicks moved in minus chicks moved out; breeding year held fixed in a model containing linear and squared dose terms

stats.unit: individual chick alive and measured at day 14 with nonmissing net_rearing_manipulation

rows.note: Outcome: mean day-14 tarsus length (mm) among measured chicks within each rearing brood. Analysis included the 332 experimentally manipulated rearing broods identified by rear_nest_breed_ID (167 enlarged and 165 reduced), comprising 2,801 chick measurements; unmanipulated broods were excluded. Each rearing brood was weighted equally. The fitted effect is the unadjusted difference in brood-mean tarsus length between enlarged and reduced arms, with a Welch unequal-variance standard error. Test statistic: Welch t = -8.39498691077; Satterthwaite inferential df = 305.225579023. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation. Enlarged mean = 16.5282206709 mm; reduced mean = 16.9165266955 mm.
rows.predictor: Sibling-competition contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt = 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt = 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); coefficient is exactly enlarged minus reduced.

rows.note: Outcome: mean day_14_weight (grams) among chicks alive and measured at day 14, computed separately for each rearing brood identified by rear_nest_breed_ID. Included experimentally manipulated broods with rear_nest_trt 5 or 6 and nonmissing day-14 mass and rearing-brood ID; excluded unmanipulated rear_nest_trt 7. Model: brood-level weighted least squares with an intercept and the signed treatment contrast; each brood's analytic weight was its number of measured day-14 chicks. Uncertainty: HC2 heteroskedasticity-robust SE across brood observations. Native effect = -1.01408397108 g; SE = 0.0896116277067 g. Test-statistic kind and value: t = -11.3164328897; inferential residual df = 330; two-sided p = 2.61908041152e-25. Fitted n = 332 rearing broods (167 enlarged, 165 reduced), representing 2,801 chick measurements. Observation unit: rearing brood. Design: two-arm experimental brood-size manipulation; brood-level WLS enlarged-minus-reduced contrast, weighted by measured chick count. The estimate is the measured-chick-weighted mean day-14 mass in enlarged broods minus that in reduced broods (9.76268656716 g minus 10.7767705382 g).
rows.predictor: Sibling-competition treatment contrast coded +0.5 for rear_nest_trt 5 (experimentally enlarged rearing brood) and -0.5 for rear_nest_trt 6 (experimentally reduced rearing brood); its coefficient is exactly the measured-chick-count-weighted enlarged-minus-reduced difference in brood mean day-14 mass.
